mcqs.learning_point: Understand the basic idea of pressure
mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly compares the pressures exerted when the same force is applied?

options.A: A nail (small area) exerts greater pressure than a hammer head (large area).
options.B: A flat board (large area) exerts greater pressure than a needle (small area).
options.C: Pressure is independent of area, so both exert the same pressure.
options.D: A larger force always gives lower pressure regardless of area.

mcqs.answer: A nail (small area) exerts greater pressure than a hammer head (large area).
mcqs.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by area (P=F/A). With the same force, a smaller contact area gives a larger pressure, so the nail produces higher pressure than the hammer head. The other options ignore the role of area or misstate the relationship.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate pressure to force and area
mcqs.question: A child pushes down on a rectangular block with a force of 120 N. The contact area between the child's hand and the block is 0.03 m². What is the pressure exerted by the child on the block?
mcqs.explanation: Pressure is calculated using P = F/A. Substituting the values gives P = 120 N / 0.03 m² = 4000 Pa. The other options result from incorrect division or misplaced decimal points.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain why sharp objects exert greater pressure
mcqs.question: Why does a sharp knife cut more easily than a blunt one?

options.A: Because the sharp knife has a smaller contact area, leading to higher pressure for the same applied force.
options.B: Because the sharp knife is made of harder material.
options.C: Because the sharp knife is lighter.
options.D: Because the sharp knife uses a different cutting motion.

mcqs.answer: Because the sharp knife has a smaller contact area, leading to higher pressure for the same applied force.
mcqs.explanation: Cutting ability depends on pressure (P=F/A). A sharp knife’s tip has a very small area, so even a modest force creates a large pressure that can overcome the material’s resistance. Material hardness or weight are not the primary reasons in this context.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes pressure in a liquid at a given depth?

options.A: Pressure increases with depth because the weight of the liquid above adds to it.
options.B: Pressure is the same at all depths because liquids are incompressible.
options.C: Pressure decreases with depth because liquid expands.
options.D: Pressure depends only on the surface area of the container.

mcqs.answer: Pressure increases with depth because the weight of the liquid above adds to it.
mcqs.explanation: In a liquid, pressure at depth h is given by P = ρgh, showing that pressure grows linearly with depth due to the weight of the fluid column above. The other statements ignore this relationship.

mcqs.question: Atmospheric pressure is best described as:

options.A: The pressure exerted by the weight of the air above a given point.
options.B: The pressure inside a sealed container.
options.C: The pressure exerted by water in a lake.
options.D: The pressure caused by wind speed.

mcqs.answer: The pressure exerted by the weight of the air above a given point.
mcqs.explanation: Atmospheric pressure results from the weight of the column of air overhead. It is distinct from pressures inside containers, hydrostatic pressure in liquids, or dynamic pressure from wind.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday example of pressure being used to lift a heavy object?

options.A: Using a hydraulic car jack to lift a car.
options.B: Using a magnet to pick up a metal nail.
options.C: Using a rope to pull a sled.
options.D: Using a battery to power a flashlight.

mcqs.answer: Using a hydraulic car jack to lift a car.
mcqs.explanation: A hydraulic jack works on Pascal’s principle: a small force applied to a small-area piston creates a large pressure that is transmitted to a larger-area piston, producing a large lifting force. The other options involve magnetism, tension, or electrical energy, not pressure.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the basic idea of pressure
mcqs.question: A student stands on a small wooden block (area 0.02 m²) with a weight of 500 N. What is the pressure exerted on the floor by the block?
mcqs.explanation: Pressure = Force/Area = 500 N / 0.02 m² = 25,000 Pa. The other options arise from dividing by larger areas or misplacing the decimal point.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate pressure to force and area
mcqs.question: If a gardener wants to water plants using a hose that delivers water at a pressure of 200 kPa, and the nozzle opening has an area of 0.001 m², what is the force exerted by the water on the nozzle?
mcqs.explanation: Force is obtained from F = P × A. Converting 200 kPa to pascals gives 200,000 Pa. Multiplying by the area: 200,000 Pa × 0.001 m² = 200 N. The other options result from incorrect unit conversion or arithmetic.
